newsitem.title: UK: IPE Brent ends steady as U.S. stifles early bounce.
newsitem.headline: IPE Brent ends steady as U.S. stifles early bounce.

text.p: IPE Brent crude futures ended unchanged on Thursday as an early rebound from Wednesday's 31-cent slide petered out with U.S. markets failing to take up the baton, dealers said.
"We needed the U.S. to confirm the bounce and it didn't happen," said a broker.
August Brent crude closed at $17.77 a barrel after finding support at Wednesday's low of $17.68 and psychological resistance just below $18.
"The market failed on the upside so it came back and took another look at yesterday's low," said a broker.

Dealers said the interrupted session - trading was suspended for 17 minutes due to a fire alert in the basement of the IPE building -- started brightly but Brent was unable to break out of the range given the bearish backdrop of U.S. oversupply.
Providing fundamental support were fears of delays in the resumption of Iraqi exports under the U.N.'s oil-for-food plan.
A proposal by Britain and the United States to impose new sanctions on Iraq for blocking U.N. weapons inspection teams several times this month also lent the market some assistance.
The measures would include preventing Iraqi officials from travelling abroad and suspending reviews of trade sanctions.
Next week's Organisation of Petroleum Exporting Countries (OPEC) meeting in Vienna was also deterring some players from taking new positions.
Earlier, IPE gas oil futures closed slightly higher but spot market weakness threatened to push prices lower again.
July IPE gas oil settled 75 cents higher at $159.50 a tonne, having shed $5 on Wednesday.
European spot gas oil markets are feeling the weight of incoming cargoes from Russia, the Mediterranean and even from across the Atlantic.
